lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 3 you met light and shadows. How is a shadow made? Something blocks the light.
Earth spins once a day. The side facing the Sun has day; the side facing away has night.
As Earth spins, the Sun seems to move across the sky: rising in the east and setting in the west. Shadows move and change length.
Shadows are long in the morning and evening, when the Sun is low, and shortest around midday, when it is highest.
Earth also travels round the Sun once a year. As it does, we see different stars at night in different seasons.

Try it in the world: stand a post in your world and mark the end of its shadow in the morning, at midday and in the evening. When is it shortest? Next, in grade 8: the Moon's phases, eclipses and seasons.

exercises.prompt: What causes day and night?
exercises.hint: Earth turns once a day.
exercises.explain: Earth spins, so each side faces the Sun, then faces away.

exercises.prompt: Where does the Sun rise?
exercises.hint: It sets in the west.
exercises.explain: The Sun rises in the east.

exercises.prompt: Shadows are shortest around midday.
exercises.hint: When is the Sun highest?
exercises.explain: Yes: the Sun is highest around midday.

exercises.prompt: How long does Earth take to spin once?
exercises.hint: Think of the Sun rising, setting and rising again. How long does that take?
exercises.explain: One spin takes one day.

exercises.prompt: The Sun really moves across the sky while Earth stays still.
exercises.hint: What is really moving?
exercises.explain: No: Earth spins, so the Sun only seems to move.

exercises.prompt: When are shadows longest?
exercises.hint: When is the Sun low?
exercises.explain: When the Sun is low, shadows are long.

exercises.prompt: How long does Earth take to travel round the Sun?
exercises.hint: It makes the seasons.
exercises.explain: One trip round the Sun takes a year.

exercises.prompt: Order a tree's shadow through the day, from 8 am.
exercises.hint: The Sun rises in the east.
exercises.explain: Morning: long and west; midday: short; evening: long and east.

exercises.prompt: We see different stars at night in winter and in summer.
exercises.hint: Earth moves round the Sun.
exercises.explain: Yes: as Earth travels round the Sun, the night side faces different stars.

exercises.prompt: It is day in London. Where is it night?
exercises.hint: Half of Earth faces away from the Sun.
choices: on the other side of Earth
exercises.explain: The side facing away from the Sun has night.

exercises.prompt: A shadow points west. Where is the Sun?
exercises.hint: Shadows point away from the light.
exercises.explain: Shadows point away from the Sun, so it is in the east: morning.

exercises.prompt: Why do we see some star groups only in winter?
exercises.hint: Earth travels round the Sun.
choices: Earth's night side faces them only then.
exercises.explain: Through the year, our night side faces different parts of space.

exercises.prompt: At midday your shadow is at its longest.
exercises.hint: Where is the Sun at midday?
exercises.explain: No: at midday the Sun is highest, so shadows are shortest.

exercises.prompt: A sundial uses a shadow to tell the time. Why does it work?
exercises.hint: Shadows move as Earth spins.
choices: The shadow moves in a pattern each day.
exercises.explain: The shadow moves the same way every day, so it shows the time.

exercises.prompt: A graph shows a pole's shadow: long at 9, short at 12, long at 3. What pattern is this?
exercises.hint: Compare 12 with 9 and 3.
choices: shortest when the Sun is highest
exercises.explain: The shadow is shortest at midday, when the Sun is highest.

exercises.prompt: Match each time to the pole's shadow.
exercises.hint: The Sun rises in the east, is highest at midday, and sets in the west. Shadows point away from it.
exercises.explain: Early morning: the Sun is in the east, so a long shadow points west. Midday: short. Evening: the Sun is in the west, so a long shadow points east.

exercises.prompt: Sort each one: caused by Earth spinning, or by Earth going round the Sun?
items: the Sun rising in the east
exercises.hint: One spin takes a day; one trip round the Sun takes a year.
exercises.explain: Day and night, sunrise and moving shadows come from Earth spinning. The different stars of each season and a year passing come from Earth going round the Sun.

exercises.prompt: Sort the times: is the Sun low (long shadows) or high (short shadows)?
exercises.hint: The Sun is highest around midday and lowest near sunrise and sunset.
exercises.explain: Early in the morning (6 am, 8 am) and in the evening (7 pm) the Sun is low, so shadows are long. Around midday and 1 pm it is high, so shadows are short.

exercises.prompt: Order the Sun's path across the sky in one day.
exercises.hint: Where does the Sun rise, and where does it set?
exercises.explain: The Sun rises in the east, is highest around midday, and sets in the west. It only seems to move: Earth spins towards the east.

exercises.prompt: Order a pole's shadow from the shortest to the longest.
exercises.hint: The further from midday, the lower the Sun and the longer the shadow.
exercises.explain: At midday the Sun is highest: the shortest shadow. By 2 pm it is a little lower, and by 6 pm it is low in the west: the longest shadow, pointing east.
